messages:
Aisha: Quick sync — I pushed a prototype of the role-scoping editor to the feature branch. Main goals: let admins create roles that are route-aware (eg. generate:write but deny model-admin), show effective quotas per role, and surface audit keys for telemetry. Can we call out any tricky enforcement edge cases?

Ken: Nice. Two quick ones: 1) scope intersection vs union semantics when a user belongs to multiple scopes (team + project) — need deterministic resolution. 2) quota propagation when a role is bounded to a subset of models (do we show per-role remaining tokens or only per-user?)

Lina: For 1) we should do intersection for allow rules (i.e., user needs an allow from both scope and role?) — that ends up being least surprising for enterprise customers who expect conservative defaults. For 2) show both: per-role committed quota (project-level) + per-user live usage. UI can fold per-user under an accordion.

Aisha: Good call. Conservative default = safer. UX question: how do we let admins preview "effective permissions" for a chosen user before applying? I sketched a preview pane that runs a dry-run against the internal policy engine. Thoughts on the internal API shape?

Owen: API shape should be small and idempotent: POST /policy/dry-run {principal, resource, action, context}. Return decision + explain list of matched rules + telemetry keys. Example response I[0m want: allow|deny, matched_rules: [...], metrics_key.

Ken: Love the dry-run. Also we need to include rollout flags: staged vs immediate, and an audit toggle. Enterprises will ask for "apply in canary to a subset of org". Maybe include targeting by org-id and percentage.

Lina: UX nit: when defining a role scope, we should let admins choose "inherit from parent org" or "lock at this level". If locked, no downstream can widen scope. Add a small lock icon.

Aisha: Agreed. On enforcement: do we rely on the API gateway to reject unauthorized requests, or keep enforcement within the service mesh? Pros/cons?

Owen: Gateway enforcement is nice for early rejection (cheap), but it'll need to be highly available and synchronized with latest policy. Service-level enforcement is authoritative and can access model/context (eg token counts). Proposed pattern: Gateways do fast allow/deny for route+principal, then backend performs a final policy check for sensitive ops (model deploy, key rotation, quota debit).

Ken: Sounds right. We'll need a sync mechanism: versioned policy blobs and a short TTL cache. Also, telemetry needs consistent decision_id across gateway+backend so traces correlate.

Lina: For telemetry, include fields: decision_id, matched_rule_ids, policy_version, evaluation_time_ms, actor_id, resource_id, action, outcome. That will let us build an "effective permissions" timeline in Console.

Aisha: I've mocked the policy JSON in the branch. Example snippet in the comment:

```
{
  "policy_version": "2026-01-12-v1",
  "rules": [
    {"id":"r1","effect":"allow","actions":["generation.create"],"resources":["models/*/versions/*"],"scopes":[{"org":"org_123","teams":["team_a"]}]},
    {"id":"r2","effect":"deny","actions":["model.admin"],"resources":["models/*"],"scopes":[{"org":"org_123"}]}
  ]
}
```

Aisha: Note r1 is scoped to team_a only, r2 denies model.admin at org level. Dry-run should show both matched rules and final allow/deny.

Owen: Small implementation note: deny precedence must be explicit in the engine. Make matching deterministic: collect all matched rules, if any explicit deny -> deny, else if explicit allow -> allow, else default deny. Document in spec.

Ken: Migration plan: customers with old "roles" table should have a one-click converter in Console that maps into new policy JSON with heuristics. We also provide an "audit report" showing any gaps or widened access post-migration.

Lina: Can we expose labels on rules for SSO-driven sync? e.g., rule.label = "security:high" so SSO connectors can map AD groups to policy-scopes automatically.

Aisha: Good idea. Also need to show quota consumption in the role editor: example display "Committed quota: 1M tokens / month — Current burn: 123k" and a link to per-route breakdown.

Ken: UX edge: when a role is tied to dedicated capacity (reserved GPU), we should show estimated cost impact if you grant generate:high-throughput to many users. Possibly a "cost simulator" in the preview pane.

Owen: On the API debate, one more: Should policy CRUD be part of the existing tenancy service or a new policy-service? My vote: separate service with thin tenancy auth. Easier to iterate and scale.

Lina: Separate service + versioned blobs + webhook for changes sounds clean. Console subscribes to change events for live preview.

DeployBot: deploy:policy-service v0.3.2 pushed to staging at 1758432400 — dry-run endpoint available at /policy/dry-run.

Aisha: Great — can folks run the dry-run against sample users and paste results here? I'll iterate the UI after we validate the explainability output.

Ken: Running it now against user: owen@example.com...

Owen: Result: deny — matched_rules: [r2], decision_id: dec_0a1b2c, eval_ms: 12. Paste below if helpful.

Ken: Paste: `\{"outcome\":\"deny\",\"matched_rules\":\[\"r2\"\],\"decision_id\":\"dec_0a1b2c\",\"policy_version\":\"2026-01-12-v1\"}`

Lina: Looks good. Next steps: Aisha iterate UI mockups with preview pane + cost simulator, Ken write migration heuristics, Owen wire gateway sync and decision_id propagation, I'll draft telemetry schema doc. We'll sync tomorrow 10am. :calendar: Done? :thumbsup:

Aisha: :thumbsup: Thanks everyone, will post updated screenshots here before the meeting.
